supporting_observations.claim: WS-LMARTINS-01 made repeated proxy CONNECT requests to updates.pixelforge-suite.co at approximately five-minute intervals from 13:37 through 14:07 UTC; the proxy returned status 200 for each request.

The periodic proxy connections are attributed by endpoint network records to pfupdater.exe running from Leo Martins's user-writable AppData\Roaming\PixelForge directory, rather than the inventory's approved C:\Program Files\PixelForge path. The logged destination also ends in .co rather than the inventory's approved .com. These discrepancies are suspicious but do not alone prove maliciousness.
The same process wrote to its own executable path shortly after starting. This is relevant for review but does not establish whether the write was a legitimate updater operation or tampering.

Dropbox and Google Drive startup processes were launched in Leo Martins's user session. Those services are not approved in the supplied inventory, but these records do not show that either process made network connections or transferred files.
The supplied proxy records show Firefox accessing portal.azure.com with successful responses, distinct from the periodic PixelForge-named connections.

known_telemetry_limitations: The stated winsec and Sysmon collection outage is limited to WS-NBLAKE-01 from 13:30 to 14:10 UTC; the supplied coverage status reports those sensors available on WS-LMARTINS-01, and proxy and Zeek coverage available for all hosts.
The supplied periodic-connection records show proxy CONNECT tunnels, not the updater traffic's TLS contents, requested paths, downloaded files, or payload.
The evidence supplied does not include a hash, signature-validation result, provenance, or detailed file analysis for the AppData\Roaming\PixelForge\pfupdater.exe binary.
claims_not_established: Whether updates.pixelforge-suite.co is controlled by PixelForge, is an authorized endpoint, or is malicious.

Whether Dropbox or Google Drive made network connections or were used to transfer organizational data.
Whether the executable-path write was a normal self-update or an unauthorized modification.
additional_evidence_needed: Acquire and analyze the updater binary, including hash, signature status, file provenance, and comparison with a known-good PixelForge release.
Verify the logged .co hostname against vendor documentation and DNS, certificate, and domain-reputation evidence; obtain relevant proxy TLS metadata if available.
Review endpoint file and process activity around the updater's execution and self-write, including any files it created, modified, or accessed.
Check proxy and endpoint telemetry for Dropbox or Google Drive connections and any associated file transfers.
Confirm with Leo Martins and the software owner whether the AppData-based updater and the .co destination were authorized.
